govdocs-archive_org-TridentineMassAlfons: Alfons Cardinal Stickler’s Attractiveness of the Tridentine Mass pleads for the old Latin rite. The Austrian cardinal’s learned pages back the traditional Mass. His red hat lent weight to the cause. The old rite endures today. The book is prized by old-Mass folk.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CIAOnassisArist: Charles R. Babcock’s piece — CIA, Nixon Reportedly Approved ’54 Campaign Against Onassis — covers the campaign against the shipping magnate. Old operations surface in the press. The file belongs to the intelligence archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FBIReleases12-7: This FBI teletype from Dallas — November 26, 1963 — is a Bureau wire. Dallas wired Washington daily after the killing. The declassified message is a primary source. The wire may hold a clue. Researchers value such files. The file belongs to the assassination archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-GallenRichardPo: This letter to Raphaela Seroy — November 3, 1994, creator unknown — is an archive item. The file’s full context is unclear. Letters capture voices the record misses. Its subject seems to be the JFK case. Archivists value such fragments. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-NewOrleansCouri: Russell Ellwood’s letter to Harold Weisberg — June 17, 1975 — is a researcher’s note. Researchers traded findings by mail. The letter may hold a clue. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
the-last-american-a-fragment-from-the-jo: John Ames Mitchell's Last American imagines Persian explorers finding a ruined, empty America — a fragment from the journal of Khan-Li. This 1889 satire of civilization was startlingly ahead of its time. A forgotten classic of early science fiction. Its vision of fallen greatness still gives readers pause.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agostini-agaz: A 1913 entry on Agostino Agazzari — the Sienese composer of the early Baroque. James Völker notes his sacred music. His Del sonare sopra il basso taught continuo. Siena's maestro left lasting works. Music's new age, in Tuscan dress. His madrigals charmed the Sienese court.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alatri: A 1913 entry on Alatri — the Italian diocese of the Cyclopean walls. Ernesto Buonaiuti gives its story. Its acropolis predates Rome itself. Bishops have watched from its heights. An ancient see on older stones. Its walls defy the archaeologists' dating. Its cathedral keeps a Eucharistic miracle.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alessandro-se: This 1913 reference article on Alessandro Serpieri — the Jesuit astronomer and seismologist. John Stein honors his science. His observatory watched the Italian skies. Faith and physics met in his work. A priest among the scientists. His earthquake studies aided Italian science.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-allori: This 1913 reference piece on the Allori — Alessandro and Cristofano, Florentine painters. Augustus Van Cleef honors father and son. Their Mannerist grace filled the palaces. The Uffizi keeps their finest. A family's century of art. Their portraits line the Pitti walls.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anselmo-bandu: A 1913 entry on Anselmo Banduri — the Benedictine numismatist. Maurice Hassett honors his coin studies. His volumes mapped the imperial mints. Florence's library housed his labors. A monk among the antiquaries. His coins grace the Florence cabinets. His Imperium graced the imperial press.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antivari: A 1913 entry on Antivari — Bar, the Montenegrin archdiocese. Elisabeth Christitch tells its border story. Its archbishops faced the Ottoman power. The Adriatic guards its old town. A see of the Balkan shore. Its primate wears the pallium still. Its coast saw the Venetian galleys.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-alleg: This 1913 reference article on Correggio — Antonio Allegri, the painter of grace. Leigh Hunt praises his Parma domes. His light melts the sacred scenes. No hand was softer or sweeter. The magician of the brush. His Io charms the Vienna gallery.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-neri: This 1913 reference article on Antonio Neri — the priest of the glassmaker's art. Edward Phillips notes his Arte Vetraria. His book taught the furnace's secrets. Florence's glass owed him its hues. A priest among the craftsmen. His recipes colored the Venetian glass.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-strad: A 1913 entry on Antonio Stradivari — the master violin maker of Cremona. Elizabeth Lorkin honors his matchless craft. His instruments sing three centuries on. No maker ever matched his varnish. The prince of the luthiers. His Messiah rests in Oxford's case.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bari: This 1913 reference piece on Bari — the archdiocese of St. Nicholas. Umberto Benigni honors its famous shrine. The saint's bones rest in its crypt. The Normans built the great basilica. The see of the sailor's saint. Its old town faces the Adriatic.
